key_insight: Using a reverse-predictivity test (predicting ANN unit activity from primate brain responses), the authors show that only a subset of ANN units align with primate neural responses, revealing substantial misalignment between ANNs and brains despite strong bidirectional alignment between two primate brains.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether ANN–brain correspondence is truly bidirectional and identifies that many model units do not have neural counterparts, resolving ambiguity about how well ANNs match biological neural responses at the unit level.
method: Reverse predictivity: predict individual ANN unit responses from recorded primate brain responses (the reverse of typical model→brain mapping).
Compare bidirectional alignment: quantify and contrast reverse and forward predictivity between ANN↔brain and brain↔brain (two primates).
Unit- and layer-level analysis to identify which subset of ANN units align with brain responses and measure overall misalignment.
impact: Provides a more rigorous, bidirectional benchmark for model–brain comparisons that exposes gaps in current ANN similarity to biological brains—guiding model design, evaluation, and unit-level interpretability for brain-inspired AI.
visual_elements: Heatmap of reverse predictivity scores across ANN units and layers (highlight aligned subset).
Scatterplot comparing forward vs reverse predictivity per unit, with aligned/non-aligned regions marked.
Schematic diagram of bidirectional mappings: brain↔brain (strong, thick arrows) vs brain↔ANN (sparser, thinner arrows).
Bar chart showing proportion of ANN units aligned vs non-aligned and comparison to brain–brain alignment baseline.
paper_title: Reverse predictivity for bidirectional comparison of neural networks and biological brains
